import numpy as np

def move(terrain, start, duration_s, n_runs, seed):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)

    n_steps = 60
    dt = duration_s / (n_steps - 1)
    points = np.empty((n_runs, n_steps, 3), dtype=float)
    points[:, 0, :2] = start
    points[:, 0, 2] = 0

    lat = np.full(n_runs, start[0])
    lon = np.full(n_runs, start[1])
    elapsed = np.zeros(n_runs)

    # Target median ~2.86 km in duration_s gives mean speed about:
    mean_speed = 2.86e3 / duration_s  # m/s
    # Use base pace close to mean speed slowed by slope.
    # Base speed (flat) around 1.1 m/s
    base_speed = 1.1

    cell_m = terrain.cell_m
    m_lat = terrain.m_lat
    m_lon = terrain.m_lon

    # Bearings variation: mostly southward with some noise
    # South = -90 degrees = -pi/2 rad
    base_bearing = -np.pi/2
    bearing_noise = rng.normal(0, np.pi/9, n_runs)  # ±20 degrees noise
    bearing = base_bearing + bearing_noise  # initial bearing

    # We will update bearing each step to follow descent direction with noise
    # If terrain slope is too steep, reduce step length accordingly

    # Precompute step times (same for all runs) for steady timestamps
    times = np.linspace(0, duration_s, n_steps)

    for i in range(1, n_steps):
        # Compute elevation gradient approx by small offset north and south
        delta = 0.0001  # ~11m lat
        lat_n = lat + delta
        lat_s = lat - delta

        elev_n = terrain.elev(lat_n, lon)
        elev_s = terrain.elev(lat_s, lon)
        elev_c = terrain.elev(lat, lon)

        # Approximate slope south-north: negative means descending south
        slope_ns = (elev_s - elev_n)/(2 * delta * m_lat)  # m/m

        # East-west slope approx to add noise to bearing
        lon_e = lon + delta
        lon_w = lon - delta
        elev_e = terrain.elev(lat, lon_e)
        elev_w = terrain.elev(lat, lon_w)
        slope_ew = (elev_e - elev_w)/(2 * delta * m_lon)  # m/m

        # The subject tends to move downhill southward, so adjust bearing towards south if slope_ns negative (downhill south)
        # Compute bearing offsets from slope gradient (stronger slope adjust more)
        # Also add small random perturbation to simulate human path variation
        down_slope_bearing = -np.pi/2  # south

        # Combine slope direction bias and noise
        slope_strength = np.clip(-slope_ns, 0, 0.3)  # only downhill south counts, max capped for stability
        bearing_noise = rng.normal(0, np.pi/15, n_runs)  # smaller noise each step (~12deg)
        slope_bearing_adjust = slope_strength * (down_slope_bearing - bearing)
        bearing += slope_bearing_adjust + bearing_noise
        bearing = (bearing + np.pi) % (2 * np.pi) - np.pi  # wrap to [-pi, pi]

        # Compute step distance targeted for median around 2.86 km total:
        # Compute current slope deg to scale speed
        slope_deg = terrain.slope_deg(lat, lon)
        # Compute elevation diff and horizontal step to estimate speed
        # Elev change over horiz distance ~ slope in radians
        slope_rad = np.deg2rad(slope_deg)
        horiz_step = base_speed * dt * np.cos(slope_rad)
        elev_diff = base_speed * dt * np.sin(slope_rad)

        # Compute walking speed with Tobler function for realistic pacing, limit to base_speed max
        speed = terrain.tobler_speed_ms(elev_diff, horiz_step)
        # Limit unrealistic speed spikes
        speed = np.clip(speed, 0.2, 1.5)

        step_dist = speed * dt  # meters moved this step

        # Update lat/lon position by offset with current bearing
        lat, lon = terrain.offset(lat, lon, bearing, step_dist)
        # Clamp inside terrain box
        lat, lon = terrain.clamp(lat, lon)

        elapsed[:] = times[i]

        points[:, i, 0] = lat
        points[:, i, 1] = lon
        points[:, i, 2] = elapsed

    ok = terrain.inside(points[:, -1, 0], points[:, -1, 1])

    return points, ok
